definition.records: nine (phrase -> (slot, name)) rows; the key is the phrase, the value the entity

segment_c.counting: for every entity, the distinct wordings the frozen corpus supplies are enumerated; the key/entity ratio is reported at each scale it can reach, and a scale that is not admissible is reported as refused with the blocking rule
segment_c.name_rule: an entity name may never enter a key (R11 invariant), so name-bearing sentences are not writable
segment_c.distribution: per-entity key counts are reported as min / median / max at each scale

segment_d.table: 18 keys: the 9 corpus wordings plus the 9 authored aliases of R13
segment_d.read: same containment rule as R13: a record answers only when its whole sequence occurs in the query
segment_d.zeros: 12 unknown candidates, 18 byte fragments, 20 whole sentences

segment_e.rule: first writer wins: a write whose key is already bound to a different value is rejected with reason address_already_bound and the whole batch is left unapplied
segment_e.counterfactual: the same table built with on_conflict='replace' is measured and reported, not gated

criteria.segment_c: report per-entity key count min/median/max and the key/entity ratio at 9, 18 and the refused 78 keys; state whether the ratio rises and why.
criteria.segment_d: on the 18-key table: 12 unknown candidates answer 0; 18 byte fragments answer 0; 20 whole sentences mis-point 0; capability 40/40 with zero wrong pointers; nine closed-state checks.
criteria.segment_e: every adversary case exits rejected_batch_address_already_bound with the table content digest unchanged and the first binding still readable; the append control (two wordings, one entity) is accepted; a within-batch collision still exits rejected_batch_address_collision.
criteria.reporting: segments are reported separately; a clean C does not carry D or E.
